context:
Campaign context: this outreach campaign is for Relay Wichita in Wichita.

PERSONAS:
- Maya, 19, Recently exited foster care, hoping to start school (Wichita, staying at the CrossRoads youth shelter). Barriers: A state ID needs a birth certificate, a Social Security card and proof of residency, which takes at least 31 days from no documents; A monthly bus pass costs $50, and buses run 30-60 minutes apart with no Sunday service; Aged-out KanCare coverage loses 42% of youth, so her health coverage is at risk; DCF Independent Living benefits stop at age 21, whether or not she has housing or income. Reached via: CrossRoads Drop-In Center peer navigators, DCF IL caseworker referrals, Instagram and TikTok short videos, Text line for youth. Says: "I can find a bed this week. What I need is someone to walk me through my ID, my health coverage and school, step by step."
- Denise, 42, Mother of two children (Wichita, between housing). Barriers: Too many doors: 8 intake sites, and she cannot tell which one to call; A family intake queue can run 2-4 weeks, too slow for a family in crisis; Family shelter has a 90-day stay limit; Most private landlords use a 3x-rent income rule she cannot meet yet. Reached via: 211 phone line in English and Spanish, Open Door walk-in intake, Bilingual flyers at schools and clinics. Says: "I don't need more phone numbers. I need the right one, and I need someone to stay with me until my kids have a place."
- Robert, 58, Veteran (Downtown Wichita, unsheltered). Barriers: Only 17 of 87 emergency beds are reachable for people living outside; Union Rescue Mission's breathalyzer gate filters out roughly a third of would-be intakes; Bed referrals are still placed by phone because Second Light bed-matching is not live yet; City ID needs proof of Wichita residency, which unsheltered people rarely can show. Reached via: H.O.T. street outreach, Open Door daytime drop-in, VASH and veteran service partners. Says: "Tell me about a bed that fits me tonight, not a bed somewhere in theory."

CHANNEL PLAN:
- Youth peer outreach at CrossRoads and DCF IL: audience Youth ages 18-24 aging out of foster care; content Pocket ID checklist, document-steps comic, peer navigator talks; Weekly drop-in sessions plus every new DCF IL case; KPI Youth who start a birth-certificate or ID request within 7 days; reach 300 youth
- 211 and Open Door bilingual front-door scripts: audience Families and adults calling or walking in, English and Spanish; content Bilingual call scripts, wallet cards, text follow-ups; Daily, every call and walk-in; KPI Share of contacts with a confirmed warm handoff; reach 2,000 people
- H.O.T. street outreach kits: audience Unsheltered adults and veterans; content Weatherproof cards with tonight's reachable beds, water bottles with the Relay text line; Every outreach shift, weekdays; KPI Street contacts referred to a bed that fits them; reach 195 people
- NEXTenant landlord briefings: audience Wichita landlords and property managers; content Landlord breakfasts, risk-guarantee fact sheet, named contact card; Every 2 weeks; KPI New landlords signed to NEXTenant; reach 150 landlords
- Instagram, TikTok and Facebook: audience Youth, families and the wider community; content Short real-story videos, myth-busting posts, Spanish captions; 4 posts a week; KPI Text-line sign-ups from social posts; reach 25,000 impressions
- Transit center posters and Spanish radio: audience Bus riders and Spanish-speaking households; content Bilingual posters, radio spots, QR code to the pathway; Posters all 90 days; radio weekly; KPI QR scans and radio-driven calls; reach 15,000 people

KPIs:
- People connected to a housing pathway with a named contact: 120 (Year 1)
- Contacts handed off live to the next service, not just given a number: 80% (By day 90)
- Days from intake to a birth-certificate request for youth with no documents: 3 days (By day 90)
- New landlords signed to NEXTenant: 15 (By day 90)
- Pathway contacts served in Spanish: 20% (By day 90)
- Youth who lose contact with their navigator, down from DCF IL's 38%: 20% (By day 90)

BRIEF — QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS (the competition's own items and this page's answers):
- Q: Youth-friendly outreach kit
  A: The youth kit goes out through CrossRoads, DCF IL and BRIDGES, led by peer navigators with lived experience. It holds a pocket ID checklist that turns the 31-day document chain into plain steps, a bus-pass voucher guide, and a KanCare keep-your-coverage card. The goal is to cut lost contact below 20%, against DCF IL's 38%.
- Q: Landlord trust campaign
  A: Landlord Luis asked for one clear contact, less risk and support that lasts, so every NEXTenant landlord gets a named Relay contact and a fact sheet on rapid rehousing and Housing First supports. We run landlord briefings every 2 weeks and aim to sign 15 new landlords by day 90. We will share Wichita's retention rate of 80% to show tenants stay housed.
- Q: Bilingual pathway messaging
  A: Every script, wallet card, flyer and text message is written in English and Spanish at a 6th-grade level. 211 and Open Door already support Spanish, so Relay builds on them with Spanish radio spots and transit posters. The target is 20% of contacts served in Spanish.
- Q: Anti-stigma comms
  A: The anti-stigma series tells real stories from youth, parents and veterans, with their consent. It points out that 69% of people served were newly homeless, so homelessness can happen to any neighbor. Messages focus on what people are working toward, like school, a job and a home, not on labels.
- Q: Brand system
  A: Relay Wichita uses a baton-handoff mark to show that no person is dropped between services. The brand has a warm color set, plain bilingual wording and the handle @RelayWichita, with co-branding space for Second Light, Open Door, H.O.T., CrossRoads, BRIDGES, DCF IL, City ID and NEXTenant. The promise is simple: every door leads home.
- Q: Channel plan and budget
  A: The $100K marketing reserve is split across youth peer outreach and kits at $25,000, landlord briefings at $20,000, bilingual front-door scripts and print at $15,000, anti-stigma video at $15,000, social media at $15,000, and brand design at $10,000. Channels favor partners, phones and social media because many people in crisis lack a carro or reliable transit. Each channel has its own KPI that is tracked on the pilot dashboard.
